_about: Words for the guided tour that only a person can supply: what the facade really is, how the way in works, and how sure we are of the position. Everything else in the tour is generated from the workbook and the measured walks (jindalx/build-data.cjs). 'basis' is shown on screen: workbook, measured, assumed, unverified or verified. Update a line, and its basis, as soon as a fact is confirmed. Updated 24 November 2026 after the check against Google satellite and Street View (docs/JINDALX_VERIFICATION.md).

overview.title: Magnus Towers · Sector 67
overview.text: Six floors above ground and a basement, 38,000 sq ft a floor: the largest plate of the four. The only new building on the list, with handover due in December 2026.

facade.text: We checked this against 2026 imagery. The real building is a long, low block with white stone and plaster at the base, glazed lobby bays, dark glass bands and white aluminium fascias, and it is still being glazed. The model you see is our earlier guess, a glass tower, and is being redrawn.

approach.text: On wider roads in a part of Sector 67 that is not dense, with sufficient parking, the sheet says. In the imagery the road front is a continuous boundary wall behind a belt of trees; the likely vehicle gate is on the east road, and the landlord should confirm it.

position.text: The sheet's pin is a road junction. Google places Magnus Greens, plot C-2, about 520 metres south-east, and the model stands in the wrong place. Plot plan and gates must come from the landlord.

overview.title: A104 · Sector 4
overview.text: Stilt ground floor and three floors above, with a basement, 25,000 sq ft a floor. The sheet calls it new, with handover due in December 2026.

facade.text: The model shows painted plaster. The best match in the imagery is a dark-grey panel and glass block of four levels, with black sunshade fins, but no public page confirms which building is A-104. Treat this facade as unknown until the landlord sends a photo.

approach.text: The sheet says one approach road is narrow and the other has a dump yard. The imagery agrees: a narrow lane about ten metres wide with a guarded steel gate on one side, and a garbage heap on the wide road on the other.

position.text: The pin is only the centre of Sector 4. The model stands on small shops, so its position is wrong. The likely building is about 140 metres west, and the landlord must confirm it.

overview.title: A14/18/19 · Sector 9
overview.text: Stilt ground floor and four floors: the lower three at 18,000 sq ft, the top two at 8,000. The whole building is available, and it is being upgraded.

facade.text: The model shows painted plaster. The imagery shows something else on Amaltash Marg: a new glass and copper-toned panel front, with an open stilt floor and scaffolding at one edge, so the upgrade is under way. The model is being redrawn.

approach.text: On a main road with a good link to the DND road, the sheet says. In the imagery the entrance is on the divided Amaltash Marg frontage; the lane behind is not confirmed as part of the building.

position.text: The real A-14 front is about 110 metres from where the model stands, and its frontage is about 13 metres, so the sheet's 18,000 sq ft a floor must include neighbouring plots. The landlord must supply the plot lines.

overview.title: D1 · Sector 3
overview.text: Ground floor and two floors above, 20,000 sq ft a floor. The whole building is available, and it is being upgraded.

facade.text: The model shows plain plaster. The building we believe is D-1 is cream plaster with large teal windows, some arched, a green glass bay and a round glazed corner tower, behind a wall with sliding gates. It reads as three or four levels, not two. Identity is not yet confirmed.

approach.text: A street of about 13 metres runs along the long face and a second along the end, with a gate on each in the imagery. The sheet says approach roads are wider.

position.text: The model stands about 140 metres from the building we believe is D-1. It rests on third-party place data, and no name plate was read, so the landlord must confirm it.
